traps.why: Without AlCl₃ the OXYGEN is acylated (an ester). The ring ketone needs AlCl₃ (or the Fries rearrangement of the ester).
The OH (or the ester oxygen) is never lost: the acyl group adds to a ring C–H ortho/para to the oxygen and the OH stays on the ring.

explanation: With AlCl₃ the acylium ion attacks the ring para (or ortho when para is blocked) to the OH: a hydroxyaryl ketone. The Fries rearrangement of an aryl ester gives the same product.
tip: AlCl₃ → C-acylation (ketone), OH kept. Pyridine → O-acylation (ester).
